sources.quote: Having just graduated from the federal technical university (ETH) in Zurich, Ammann traveled to New York in hopes of gaining some practical experience in designing steel bridges.
In 1911, Ammann began working for Gustav Lindenthal, then considered the "master of long span design" (7);
Ammann thus joined, in 1925, the staff at the Port Authority as bridge engineer.
In 1924, Ammann unveiled his proposals for the bridge, a smaller, simpler and, at $40 million, decidedly less costly version of Lindenthal's crossing.
a year later this rather irascible Austrian American bridge builder made him chief engineer on the project to construct a large railroad crossing, the Hell Gate.

Most of his major bridges-the George Washington, Bayonne, Triborough, Little Hell Gate, Bronx-Whitestone, Harlem River Pedestrian as well as the Lincoln Tunnel-were built (or at least designed) during this period.
